**[The role of mitochondrial DNA and RNA in promoting liver disease pathogenesis.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42866016/)** *(from Hepatology / mitochondrial biology)*  
*Raj Sanjeevani; Warhade Anjali; Kumari Nikkee; Pandey Shweta; Babuta Mrigya* — Frontiers in cell and developmental biology 2026  
Score: **7/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, NLRP3, VDAC1, POLG-mtDNA, mito-ROS-NF-kB, NF-kB-NLRP3-priming, clinical-phenotype, other`  
> This review of mtDNA/mtRNA release (mPTP, VDAC oligomerization) and its sensing by cGAS, NLRP3, TLR9 and other PRRs in liver disease directly parallels the Blue (VDAC1 macropore → cytosolic mtDNA → cGAS-STING) and Purple (ox-mtDNA → NLRP3) streams, and bears on hepatic steatosis/MASH in the family, but it has no SAMHD1, dNTP-pool, PNC1/2 or genetic-variant data, so it is a mechanistic background review rather than direct evidence.  
DOI: 10.3389/fcell.2026.1855694

## 🟡 Medium Relevance (Score 5–6)
*Score ≥6 auto-added to Zotero; lower scores: review manually*

**[Bergapten Alleviates Periodontitis by Suppressing NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation via Mitophagy-Induced Disruption of NEK7-NLRP3 Interaction](https://doi.org/10.3390/antiox15101304)** *(from Dentistry/periodontology (oral inflammation and natural-product pharmacology))*  
*Xiang-Bin Jia; Yu-Zhao Wang; Jiao Cao; Li-Fei Pan; Xiao-Xuan Cui* — Antioxidants 2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `NLRP3, mTOR-lysosomal, ISG15-mitophagy, mito-ROS-NF-kB, POLG-mtDNA, treatment-target`  
> The paper shows that bergapten induces mitophagy via AKT-mTOR inhibition, which lowers mtROS, disrupts NEK7-NLRP3 interaction and reduces cytosolic ox-mtDNA release, so it addresses the ox-mtDNA/NLRP3 axis and the mitophagy deficit relevant to A565T haploinsufficiency. It is a periodontitis mouse model with no SAMHD1, interferon, dNTP, or cGAS-STING data, and the mitophagy is induced through a different route than the ISG15-mediated MFN/BECN1 block, so relevance is adjacent and mechanistic. It also suggests a possible small-molecule strategy to bypass the mitophagy block and dampen NLRP3 activation, and periodontitis may link to the family's inflammatory phenotypes.  
DOI: 10.3390/antiox15101304

**[Dominant lung involvement and heterozygous IFIH1 variants.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42863753/)** *(from Pulmonology (pediatric interstitial lung disease))*  
*Rapp Christina K; Herkner Moritz; Crippa Victoria S E; Michel Kataryzna; Dauletb* — Chest 2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `AGS-spectrum, JAK-STAT, clinical-phenotype, treatment-target, other`  
> The paper shows that heterozygous IFIH1 (MDA5) gain-of-function variants cause a dominant type I interferonopathy with interstitial lung disease, and that severity tracks with GoF strength. This mirrors the SAMHD1 haploinsufficiency interferonopathy (AGS/Singleton-Merten spectrum, dominant het variants, ISG signatures, JAK inhibitor rationale) and supports the idea that heterozygous variants have graded phenotypes. It does not involve SAMHD1, cGAS-STING, mitochondria, NLRP3 or dNTP metabolism directly, so it is adjacent rather than core.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.chest.2026.10.001

**[Vitiligo Biomarker CXCL10 Correlates With Clinical Response to Ruxolitinib Cream in the Phase 2 Randomized TRuE-V Mechanism-of-Action Study.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42869214/)** *(from Dermatology (vitiligo/pigmentary disorders; topical JAK inhibitor therapy))*  
*Passeron Thierry; Lebwohl Mark; Lynde Charles; Alam Maryam Shayesteh; Laquer Viv* — The Journal of investigative dermatology 2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `JAK-STAT, poliosis-neural-crest, treatment-target, clinical-phenotype`  
> Shows that topical ruxolitinib (a JAK1/2 inhibitor) lowers IFN-γ-driven CXCL10 and restores SOX10+ melanocytes with repigmentation in vitiligo, which bears on the family's silver streak/poliosis (piebaldism/neural crest pigmentation) phenotype and supports JAK inhibition as a way to damp interferonopathy amplitude. It involves IFN-γ rather than the type I IFN cGAS-STING axis, has no SAMHD1 or mitochondrial data, and is therefore only an adjacent, indirect connection.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.jid.2026.09.857

**[Bidirectional Crosstalk Between cGAS-STING and Necroptosis: From Mitochondrial DNA Release to Inflammatory Disease](https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S649776)** *(from Pharmacology / cell death biology (drug design, necroptosis, inflammation-associated disease))*  
*Hong-Quan Wang; Zhi-Ji Wang; Hui Zhang; Zhi-Hang Yang; Shu-Lin Zhao* — Drug Design, Development and Therapy 2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, VDAC1, NF-kB-IKK, JAK-STAT, treatment-target, other`  
> This review covers mtDNA release, cGAS-STING activation, type I IFN/TNF-α synergy and the necroptosis (ZBP1/RIPK3/MLKL) feedback loop, which bears directly on Loop A (VDAC1 macropore → mtDNA → cGAS-STING → IFN-I) and on chronic interferonopathy amplification and therapeutic targeting (STING inhibitors, mitochondrial protection). It has no SAMHD1, dNTP, NLRP3 or POLG data, and necroptosis is not a defined arm of the disease model, so it counts as an adjacent mechanism, not a core one.  
DOI: 10.2147/DDDT.S649776

**[NAD+ Attenuates Neuroinflammation in Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing the cGAS- STING Pathway via Mitochondrial Homeostasis Restoration.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42870203/)** *(from Neurology (cerebrovascular/stroke neuroinflammation))*  
*Jiang Sijia; Liao Bo; Wang Guiping; Sheng Rui; Han Chong* — Molecular neurobiology 2026  
Score: **6/10** | Pathways: `cGAS-STING, treatment-target, NF-kB-IKK, mito-ROS-NF-kB, other`  
> Mouse MCAO and BV2 microglia data show that NAD+ restores mitochondrial respiration, reduces cytosolic mtDNA leakage, and suppresses cGAS-STING-TBK1 signaling in a STING-dependent manner. This mirrors the Loop A mechanism (mtDNA escape, cGAS, STING, IFN-I) and suggests NAD+ repletion as a possible mitochondria-targeted adjunct for the SAMHD1 interferon-mitochondrial syndrome, which is also relevant to the ME/CFS and neuroinflammation phenotypes. However, it is an ischemic stroke model with no SAMHD1, dNTP, VDAC1 or NLRP3 data, so the connection is indirect.  
DOI: 10.1007/s12035-026-06257-1

**[Anifrolumab for refractory autoimmune hemolytic anemia in SPENCD-associated lupus: a case-based review.](https://doi.org/10.63032/mfag9316)** *(from Rheumatology (monogenic interferonopathy, lupus, autoimmune hematology))*

DOI: 10.63032/mfag9316

*Potential specialty bridges — skim titles*

**[African swine fever virus protein R298L opposes the NF-κB signaling pathway and interferon-mediated pathway.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42863326/)** *(from Veterinary virology / viral immune evasion)*  
*Yang Zhong-Yuan; Ding Ming-Yang; Chen Xing; Ling Xiang-Hui; Fan Shuai* — Veterinary microbiology 2026  
Score: **4/10** | Pathways: `NF-kB-IKK, JAK-STAT, other`  
> The paper shows that the ASFV protein pR298L blocks IKKβ–p65 interaction in NF-κB signaling and blocks JAK1/JAK2 interaction with their substrates in IFN signaling. These are the same canonical NF-κB/IKKβ and JAK-STAT nodes in the SAMHD1 A565T model, but the work is a swine viral immune-evasion study with no SAMHD1, mitochondrial, NLRP3, cGAS-STING or dNTP content and no human disease or therapeutic link. Its only value is conceptual: it shows a viral mechanism for dampening IKKβ-p65 and JAK-STAT, which are the pathways that chronic interferonopathy hyperactivates.  
DOI: 10.1016/j.vetmic.2026.111243
